speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions. To understand what is causing this, can you describe when these symptoms first started and how they have progressed since then?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: The connection between your recent self-resolving knee pain and your camping trip in Minnesota is significant; have you noticed any specific type of rash, particularly on your palms or soles? REQUEST IMAGES: [Skin_Lesion_CloseUp]

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on your palms and wrists, combined with your recent camping trip and prior knee pain, strongly suggests a specific arthropod-borne infection. Have you noticed any tick bites on your body? REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, ESR, CRP.

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated white blood cell count confirms an active infection. Given the violaceous vesiculopustular lesions, recent camping in Minnesota, and prior knee pain, have you noticed any tick bites on your body? REQUEST TEST: ESR, CRP.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Migrans (Lyme Disease) with secondary arthritis and cutaneous manifestations. The clinical picture of recent camping in Minnesota, self-resolving monoarthritis (knee), migratory joint pain, fever, chills, malaise, and violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the hands/wrists is highly specific for Borrelia burgdorferi infection. The recent knee pain and current wrist involvement likely represent early oligoarticular Lyme arthritis. Immediate treatment with doxycycline is indicated.
